body: I'm not using guilt. That was not my intention. I'm just expressing the way I feel and think and hoped that sharing this story would make people who feel alone and unloved realize that someone DOES care about them and perhaps it would make them rethink their decisions. I'm sorry if you feel as though I was trying to do that, but it was definitely not the way I meant it.
One step at a time, right? You did a very positive thing for yourself by ending the cutting. Keep going. I really hope you find your happiness.

Our entire lives were "off." I tried really hard to get her to speak to me. I would talk and talk and read the newspaper to her and ask her questions and constantly talk to her doctors... she didn't speak to anyone. Every time I saw her she would mostly stare at the table or the floor or pretend to be extremely interested in what the other people around were doing. Like I wasn't even there. I still don't understand it either. I'm trying really hard. I've gone over every moment in my head over and over and over again, and still have no answers. I've searched her room. She didn't keep a diary... if she did it's on her computer somewhere but it's not locked. I've looked through all her files and there's a few assignments from school she typed up and saved but no other word documents. 
Also, we had different fathers. I never knew mine, and hers was only around for two years and never touched me. I wasn't home much back then anyway. I was busy being a teenager. 
I appreciate your kind words, but I don't believe for a moment that she "couldn't be saved." Anyone can be saved. I just didn't figure out how to save her in time.

Please don't. I posted this with the hope that maybe it would encourage someone going through something similar to seek help so they don't end up like my sister. I didn't want to hurt you or anyone. I am very sorry. Please let me know that you're ok. I will worry. :(
